t: The Maurya Empire, ruled from Pataliputra, was the first state to unite almost the whole Indian subcontinent.
Its centralised administration and Ashoka's edicts promoting dhamma helped carry Buddhism across Asia.
It fell apart after Ashoka's death and ended c. 185 BCE when Pushyamitra Shunga killed the last emperor, Brihadratha.
dyk: Ashoka's Lion Capital from Sarnath, carved from polished sandstone over 2,000 years ago, is today the national emblem of the Republic of India.
ev: Chandragupta Maurya overthrows the Nanda dynasty of Magadha
Chandragupta gains the north-west from Seleucus I in exchange for 500 war elephants
Ashoka conquers Kalinga, then renounces conquest by force
Ashoka dies and the empire begins a rapid decline
Pushyamitra Shunga assassinates Brihadratha, ending Maurya rule
